title: Protege sidemen Charlie Luckow and Bob Young
summary: He speaks of auditioning Charlie Luckow, taking sax man Bob Young into the union at 16, and Bob's health.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: I was 16, I used to play golf with his dad and his dad kept telling me about him so I hit him in an audition and he floored me. Charlie Luckow? Charlie Luckow. His father was a fine gentleman, he died early in life, he was the head of a finance company. Charlie will tell you, I was talking to Charlie the other day. See I'm dead to lots of those fellas. Bob Young, my first sax man, I took him in the union when he was 16. And now there's nobody like me and I'm worried about him because he's not too well. I sent him to Dr. Brown, I hope Dr. Brown finds out what's wrong with him because his sister died at 23 with cancer.
Well who was this Cooper fella?
You said it was a Cooper fella at the Grand Hotel? Oh boy. Yeah.
